name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLS_PHENOLS_AND_ETHERS_MCQ_Q01 - Physical properties and bond angle of ethers and alcohols

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding alcohols and ethers:

Statement I: The boiling point of ethanol is significantly higher than that of methoxymethane despite both having the same molecular mass.

Statement II: The \(\mathrm{C-O-C}\) bond angle in methoxymethane is slightly greater than the tetrahedral angle (\(109.5^\circ\)) due to repulsive interactions between the two bulky methyl groups.

Statement III: Ethers are completely immiscible with water because the oxygen atom of an ether cannot form hydrogen bonds with water molecules.

Which of the following is correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Physical properties such as boiling point and water solubility depend on intermolecular forces—particularly hydrogen bonding—while molecular geometry around the oxygen atom is governed by electron-pair repulsions and steric interactions between attached alkyl groups.

Step 2: Evaluation of Boiling Point Behaviour
Ethanol (\(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}\)) and methoxymethane (\(\mathrm{CH_3OCH_3}\)) both have a molecular mass of \(46\text{ u}\). However, ethanol molecules associate extensively through intermolecular \(\mathrm{O-H\cdots O}\) hydrogen bonding, whereas methoxymethane lacks a hydrogen atom attached to oxygen and therefore cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with other ether molecules. Consequently, ethanol has a much higher boiling point (\(351\text{ K}\)) than methoxymethane (\(248\text{ K}\)). Thus, the claim regarding the boiling point difference is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Bond Angle in Methoxymethane
In ethers, the oxygen atom has two bond pairs and two lone pairs in an approximately tetrahedral arrangement. Because the two methyl (\(-\mathrm{CH_3}\)) groups are bulky, the steric repulsion between them widens the \(\mathrm{C-O-C}\) bond angle to \(111.7^\circ\), which is slightly greater than the regular tetrahedral angle (\(109.5^\circ\)). Thus, the claim regarding the \(\mathrm{C-O-C}\) bond angle is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Solubility in Water
Although ethers cannot form hydrogen bonds among themselves, the lone pairs on the ether oxygen atom can act as hydrogen-bond acceptors and form hydrogen bonds with the \(\mathrm{O-H}\) hydrogens of water molecules. As a result, lower ethers such as ethoxyethane are miscible with water to an extent comparable to alcohols of similar molecular mass (for example, \(7.5\text{ g}\) per \(100\text{ mL}\) water for ethoxyethane versus \(9\text{ g}\) per \(100\text{ mL}\) water for butan-1-ol). Thus, the claim that ethers are completely immiscible with water due to an inability to form hydrogen bonds is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding the higher boiling point of ethanol over methoxymethane and the widened \(\mathrm{C-O-C}\) bond angle in methoxymethane are correct, whereas the claim that ethers are completely immiscible with water is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II, and Statement III are all correct.
Statement I and Statement II are correct, while Statement III is incorrect.
Statement I and Statement III are correct, while Statement II is incorrect.
Statement II and Statement III are correct, while Statement I is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLS_PHENOLS_AND_ETHERS_MCQ_Q02 - Acidity of phenols and hydroboration oxidation of propene

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements:

Statement I: Phenol is a stronger acid than ethanol because the phenoxide ion is stabilised by delocalisation of the negative charge over the aromatic ring, whereas in the ethoxide ion the negative charge is localised on the oxygen atom.

Statement II: The presence of an electron-withdrawing nitro group at the meta position of phenol increases its acidic strength more effectively than when the nitro group is at the para position.

Statement III: Hydroboration-oxidation of propene yields propan-1-ol as the major product, corresponding to an overall anti-Markovnikov addition of water across the double bond.

Which of the following is correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The acidic strength of alcohols and phenols depends on the polarity of the \(\mathrm{O-H}\) bond and the stability of the resulting conjugate base (alkoxide or phenoxide ion). Regioselectivity in alkene hydration via hydroboration-oxidation is governed by the steric and electronic addition of borane followed by peroxide oxidation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Phenol vs Ethanol Acidity
In phenol, the hydroxyl group is attached to a more electronegative \(sp^2\)-hybridised carbon of the benzene ring, and upon ionisation the negative charge on the phenoxide ion is delocalised over the ortho and para carbons of the aromatic ring by resonance. In contrast, the ethoxide ion has its negative charge localised solely on the oxygen atom and destabilised by the electron-releasing ethyl group. Therefore, phenol (\(\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a} = 10.0\)) is a much stronger acid than ethanol (\(\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a} = 15.9\)). Thus, the claim comparing phenol and ethanol acidity is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Nitro-Substituted Phenols
An electron-withdrawing nitro (\(-\mathrm{NO_2}\)) group increases the acidity of phenol by stabilising the phenoxide ion. This stabilisation is much more pronounced when the \(-\mathrm{NO_2}\) group is at the ortho or para position, because the negative charge delocalises directly onto the carbon bearing the nitro group, allowing additional resonance stabilisation. At the meta position, only the inductive effect operates without direct resonance delocalisation onto the nitro-bearing carbon. Hence, p-nitrophenol (\(\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a} = 7.1\)) is more acidic than m-nitrophenol (\(\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a} = 8.3\)). Thus, the claim that a meta-nitro group increases acidity more effectively than a para-nitro group is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of Hydroboration-Oxidation of Propene
When propene (\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH_2}\)) reacts with diborane (\((\mathrm{BH_3})_2\)), boron attaches to the less substituted \(sp^2\) carbon carrying more hydrogen atoms to form tripropylborane, \((\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2})_3\mathrm{B}\). Subsequent oxidation with hydrogen peroxide (\(\mathrm{H_2O_2}\)) in aqueous \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) replaces the boron atom with an \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group, yielding propan-1-ol (\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2OH}\)) in excellent yield, which corresponds to an overall anti-Markovnikov hydration. Thus, the claim regarding hydroboration-oxidation of propene is correct.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding the greater acidity of phenol over ethanol and the formation of propan-1-ol by hydroboration-oxidation of propene are correct, whereas the claim that a meta-nitro group enhances phenol acidity more than a para-nitro group is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II are correct, while Statement III is incorrect.
Statement II and Statement III are correct, while Statement I is incorrect.
Statement I and Statement III are correct, while Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I, Statement II, and Statement III are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLS_PHENOLS_AND_ETHERS_MCQ_Q03 - Ether cleavage with HI and Williamson synthesis

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding the synthesis and reactions of ethers:

Statement I: Reaction of tert-butyl methyl ether with hydrogen iodide (\(\mathrm{HI}\)) yields tert-butyl iodide and methanol as the major products because cleavage proceeds via an \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) mechanism forming a stable tertiary carbocation.

Statement II: Heating tert-butyl bromide with sodium methoxide in Williamson synthesis predominantly gives 2-methylpropene instead of tert-butyl methyl ether because methoxide acts as a strong base favouring elimination over nucleophilic substitution.

Statement III: Acid-catalysed cleavage of anisole (methoxybenzene) with concentrated \(\mathrm{HI}\) produces iodobenzene and methanol due to the partial double bond character of the \(\mathrm{O-CH_3}\) bond.

Which of the following is correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cleavage of unsymmetrical ethers by \(\mathrm{HI}\) follows either an \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) or \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) pathway depending on the stability of the carbocation intermediate and the hybridisation of the carbon attached to oxygen. In Williamson synthesis, alkoxides act as both nucleophiles and strong bases, so the structure of the alkyl halide determines whether substitution or elimination predominates.

Step 2: Evaluation of tert-Butyl Methyl Ether Cleavage
Upon protonation of tert-butyl methyl ether, \((\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{C-O-CH_3}\), by \(\mathrm{HI}\), the departure of the leaving group methanol (\(\mathrm{CH_3OH}\)) generates a highly stable tertiary carbocation, \((\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{C^+}\). Nucleophilic attack by \(\mathrm{I^-}\) on this carbocation via an \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) mechanism produces tert-butyl iodide and methanol as the major products. Thus, the claim regarding the cleavage of tert-butyl methyl ether with \(\mathrm{HI}\) is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Williamson Synthesis with a Tertiary Halide
Alkoxide ions such as \(\mathrm{CH_3O^-}\) are strong bases as well as nucleophiles. When a tertiary alkyl halide such as tert-butyl bromide, \((\mathrm{CH_3})_3\mathrm{C-Br}\), is treated with sodium methoxide, \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) substitution is sterically hindered, so elimination dominates over substitution and 2-methylpropene is formed exclusively as the major organic product. Thus, the claim regarding the reaction of tert-butyl bromide with sodium methoxide is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Anisole Cleavage with \(\mathrm{HI}\)
In anisole (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5-O-CH_3}\)), protonation gives the methylphenyl oxonium ion. The \(\mathrm{O-C_6H_5}\) bond is stronger than the \(\mathrm{O-CH_3}\) bond because the phenyl carbon is \(sp^2\) hybridised and the \(\mathrm{O-C_6H_5}\) bond possesses partial double bond character due to resonance of the oxygen lone pair with the benzene ring. Consequently, \(\mathrm{I^-}\) attacks the methyl carbon to break the weaker \(\mathrm{O-CH_3}\) bond, producing phenol and iodomethane (\(\mathrm{CH_3I}\)), not iodobenzene and methanol. Thus, the claim regarding anisole cleavage is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding the \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) cleavage of tert-butyl methyl ether with \(\mathrm{HI}\) and the elimination reaction of tert-butyl bromide with sodium methoxide are correct, whereas the claim that anisole cleavage with \(\mathrm{HI}\) yields iodobenzene and methanol is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II, and Statement III are all correct.
Statement I and Statement III are correct, while Statement II is incorrect.
Statement II and Statement III are correct, while Statement I is incorrect.
Statement I and Statement II are correct, while Statement III is incorrect.
